Equi Tri In Rec

GeometryTrianglesConstructions
Game: Watch a triangle that keeps three equal sides while the shape around it bends.
How to play: Drag the corners A, B, C or D, or focus a corner and use the arrow keys. Tick the boxes to show names, angles or guiding lines, then press Reset to start over.
Look for the math

The picture starts as a rectangle, but pull a corner and it becomes a slanted four-sided shape. The orange triangle APQ still has three equal sides. Nothing about the rectangle's right angles is needed.

Two small triangles on neighbouring sides

On side BC we build an equilateral triangle BCY, and on side CD another one, CDX. Both are turned the same way: the applet takes each side, rotates a copy of it by 60° about one end, and lets the two rays meet at the new point. X and Y move whenever a corner moves, and each small triangle always has three equal sides.

Where P and Q come from

Extend AX until it meets the line BC; that is P. Extend AY until it meets the line CD; that is Q. In a rectangle, X is the midpoint of AP and Y is the midpoint of AQ, so APQ is a copy of AXY made twice as large — a dilation with coefficient 2. For a slanted shape the multiplier changes, but AX : AP and AY : AQ stay equal. That is why XY and PQ are parallel; tick Hint to see the two lines.

Why the orange triangle cannot change shape

Write u = B − A and v = D − A, so C = A + u + v. A 60° turn takes X to A + v + R₊u and Y to A + u + R₋v. Applying R₋ to the first vector gives the second, so AXY is equilateral for any parallelogram, not just a rectangle. P and Q are the same multiple of AX and AY, so APQ is just AXY turned and enlarged: equilateral too. The logic test checks this on rectangles, every one-corner drag and hundreds of random shapes, and confirms the page's proviso — if the two small triangles are turned opposite ways, the claim fails every time. One detail the picture shows but the short wording hides: P and Q lie on the lines BC and CD, and for a very wide or tall rectangle one of them falls beyond the side itself.

Pull D far to the right and watch Q slide past C onto the extension of CD; the three sides of APQ still match.
